title: A surjective non-identity selfmap of a Hausdorff space is covered by a proper closed subset and its image

standard_prerequisites.name: The Hausdorff separation axiom and the notion of a proper closed subset
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on extremally disconnected spaces, where the counted statement occurs
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the disjoint open neighbourhoods used to define the closed subset.

core_obligations: Pick a moved point and separate it from its image: since the map is not the identity there is a point p whose image differs, and Hausdorffness gives disjoint open neighbourhoods of the two (proof lines 5580-5581).

Define the closed subset: the proof sets E to be the complement of the intersection of the first neighbourhood with the preimage of the second, which is closed and misses p and hence is proper (proof lines 5581-5582).

Cover the space: for an arbitrary point, either it lies in E or it lies in that intersection, in which case a preimage argument places its image in E, so the space is the union of E and the image of E (proof lines 5583-5586).
Conclusion: the stated proper closed subset exists (proof line 5586).
proof_roadmap: 取被 f 移动的点 p，用 Hausdorff 性取 p 与 f(p) 的不交开邻域 U、V。
令 E = X \ (U ∩ f^{-1}(V))：它闭且不含 p 故为真闭子集；任取 x，若 x ∉ E 则 x ∈ U ∩ f^{-1}(V)，于是 f(x) ∈ V，取 x 在 U 中的原像 y 使 f(y) = x 可证 x ∈ f(E)，故 X = E ∪ f(E)。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the elementary covering lemma used in the section on extremally disconnected spaces (author lemma at source lines 5572-5577, label lemma-rainwater): a surjective selfmap of a Hausdorff space that is not the identity admits a proper closed subset E with X equal to E together with its image. The proof (source lines 5579-5587) is short and explicit: it separates a moved point from its image by Hausdorffness, cuts out the closed complement of a suitable neighbourhood, and then checks the covering property point by point (proof lines 5580-5586). H2.
